comparisons.comparison: Both companies reported on their 2024 income tax benefits and effective tax rates, noting shifts from the prior year. Bank of America disclosed a decrease in the total income tax benefit to $7.6 billion in 2024 from $8.4 billion in 2023, primarily attributing this to the absence of tax benefits recorded against pretax charges for the FDIC special assessment that occurred in 2023. Goldman Sachs reported an increase in its effective income tax rate to 22.4% in 2024 from 20.7% in 2023, which it attributed to a decrease in the impact of permanent tax benefits. While both cited changes in specific tax impacts (FDIC charges vs. permanent benefits) as key drivers of their respective 2024 tax positions relative to 2023, the direction and nature of the variance differed: BAC saw a decline in absolute benefit amounts linked to one-off regulatory charges, whereas GS saw a rate increase linked to the composition of permanent benefits.

sentences.text: The income tax benefit was $7.6 billion in 2024 compared to $8.4 billion in 2023.
The decrease in the income tax benefit was primarily due to the benefits recorded against pretax charges in 2023 for the FDIC special assessment and the impact of BSBY's cessation.

The effective income tax rate for 2024 was 22.4%, up from the full year income tax rate of 20.7% for 2023, primarily due to a decrease in the impact of permanent tax benefits for 2024 compared with 2023, partially offset by changes in the geographic mix of earnings.
